title: 2004 AMC 12B Problem 17
statement: For some real numbers \(a\) and \(b,\) the equation \[8x^3 + 4ax^2 + 2bx + a = 0\] has three distinct positive roots. If the sum of the base-\(2\) logarithms of the roots is \(5,\) what is the value of \(a?\)

solutions.text:
The sum of the base-\(2\) logarithms is \(\log_2(r_1 r_2 r_3) = 5,\) so \(r_1 r_2 r_3 = 2^5 = 32.\) By Vieta’s formulas on \(8x^3 + 4ax^2 + 2bx + a,\) the product of the roots is \(-\dfrac{a}{8}.\) Thus \(-\dfrac{a}{8} = 32,\) giving \(a = -256.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The sum of \(\log_2\) of the roots equals \(\log_2\) of their product
For \(8x^3 + \cdots + a,\) the product of the roots is \(-\dfrac{a}{8}\)
